text:
jonathan: Quick intake — new candidate model 'tritonx-30b' landed from the infra bench. Can we slot basic bring-up + quant sweep this sprint? I pasted the intake answers in the doc: https://internal.redwood/models/tritonx-30b/intake :eyes:

eva: I can take perf/latency profiling. Recommend we do FP16 baseline then 8-bit+QLoRa experiments. Need a quick cost estimate for running the sweeps on ded GPUs.

sara: I can handle eval suites (chat safety, instruction-following, embeddings drift). What's the target eval battery? current suggestion: commonsense, instruction-follow, summary-fidelity, embed-sim, hallucination-check.

mike: I'll own quant infra. For scope: 8-bit + 4-bit int8-like quant + llama-cc approximate kernels. Also want to try activation compression for long context. Can we get a single checkpoint and the config?

jonathan: checkpoint and config are in the intake doc (links at bottom). TL;DR: single 30B float32 ckpt, tokenizer BPE, context 8k. No LoRA.

eva: For perf, do we target 95th p99 < 200ms for 8k prompt? That's ambitious on 30B but aim for reasonable SLOs for interactive paths.

sara: Eval priority: 1) instruction-follow, 2) hallucination-check with our 500-query set, 3) embedding drift vs. baseline-embedding-2026-01. If we see >7% regress on any primary metric we block serving.

mike: rough cost estimate: one full quant sweep (8-bit & 4-bit with 3 seeds) across 3 batches will take ~120 GPU hours on p4-like nodes. If anyone can confirm availability on dedicated pool, ping @infra.

quant-bot: [automation] created PR #4123 for quant pipeline config. CI matrix: {bits: [8,4], batch_sizes: [1,4,8], kernel: [fast, safe]}.

eva: Can we prioritize 'fast' kernel only for initial run to save time? then fallback to 'safe' if regressions.

jonathan: Agreed. Plan for this sprint: perf baseline + eval battery + 8-bit 'fast' sweep. Owners: eva perf, sara evals, mike quant infra. I'll track rollout gating in the onboarding checklist.

sara: one ask — include a small prompt-set focused on instruction-length scaling (2k/4k/8k) so we can spot regressions that only appear at long context. I'll add that to intake doc.
